newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Beecham fully acquires Nigerian Sterling.
newsitem.headline: Beecham fully acquires Nigerian Sterling.

text.p: Equities listed on the Nigerian stock exchange have been reduced by one with the completion of Smithkline Beecham's merger with Sterling Products, an official of the exchange said.
The number of equities now traded on the exchange is 183 following the delisting of Sterling Products from the daily official list.

A Lagos high court approved the merger on October 30 but traders who were afraid that transactions done on Sterling shares on or before that date would not be entertained by the registrars asked for more time to complete all the paper work.
Lodgement of Sterling shares traded on or before October 30 1996 can still be completed until November 15, according to the stockbrokers to the merger.
"This gives two weeks to Smithkline Beecham registrars who must produce new certificates by November 27, 1996," said Mike Itegboje, CEO of brokerage house TRW Stockbrokers in a statement.

"It is quite clear from discussions that many investors do not understand that mergers are time bound and not open ended," Itegboje said in response to calls for an extension to allow lodgement of Sterling shares and cash payment to shareholders who chose to opt out.
"Where an investor was not able to meet the deadline, he/she would receive Smithkline Beecham certificate which could later be sold for cash," Itegboje said.
"Similarly, any broker who could not lodge after the deadline will receive for his client Smithkline Beecham certificate," he added.
For every seven Sterling shares, shareholders are to receive four of Smithkline Beecham.
